title: regional quota grace periods and SLO-driven fail-open for limiter outages
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement a region-aware graceful degradation mode for quota enforcement when regional limiter clusters become degraded or unreachable. The goal is to preserve customer-facing SLOs (tail latency & availability) by switching to SLO-driven 'fail-open' behaviors with bounded risk, introducing configurable grace periods, and ensuring fair short-term burst absorption across tenants during recovery.
acceptance_criteria: When a regional limiter reports >=5% error rate for 30s, a region-specific grace period enters: incoming requests are admitted with best-effort local soft-credits instead of hard rejects
Grace period is bounded (configurable default 60s) and auto-terminates when limiter health metrics return below thresholds
Fairness heuristics limit per-tenant best-effort burst absorption so no single tenant consumes >X% of recovered capacity during grace period
Canary rollout for the new mode in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 for 48h with monitoring dashboards and auto rollback if rejection_rate or p99 latency regressions exceed defined SLO deltas
Fallback policy documented and unit/integration tests cover failure modes: split-brain, repeated flapping, and cross-region redirection
implementation_steps: Add limiter health service: aggregated metrics (error_rate, rpc_latency_p95, lease_miss_rate) per region
Implement grace-period admission controller that swaps token-bucket checks for local soft-credit allocator when health flag set
Introduce tenant soft-credit ledger with decay/eviction to provide fairness and avoid unlimited bursting
Wire SLO guardrails: compute permitted fail-open headroom per region from live SLO budget, not hard-coded limits
Create observability surfaces: new Grafana panels, SLO delta alerts, and synthetic traffic jobs to validate behaviors
Run chaos experiments (network partitions and limiter process kills) in staging, measure recovery and fairness
Roll out as opt-in feature flag and run a canary in eu-west-1 and us-west-2
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff sync with SRE, Runtime and Product. Agreed target SLO deltas: +1% availability tolerance, +15ms p99 latency buffer during grace periods.
2026-03-02: Health service prototype pushed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/limiter/pull/412). Exposes error_rate and lease_miss_rate via /healthz/metrics.
2026-03-05: Implemented soft-credit allocator and local ledger with eviction policy (LRU+decay). Unit tests added.

2026-03-08: Integration test failing under split-brain: two regions simultaneously entering grace mode caused cross-region burst skew. Implemented cross-region cap coordination via lightweight gossiper.
2026-03-10: Canary flag created. Dashboard draft at https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/limiter/grace-periods. Preparing staging chaos run.
Blocked: Need security signoff on soft-credit telemetry (contains tenant identifiers). Added to security review queue.
decisions: Fail-open chosen over fail-closed for limited duration because customer-facing availability per SLO is prioritized over perfect quota enforcement.
Soft-credit allocator will use a decay window (default 5 minutes) to avoid long-term state accumulation.
Grace period default set to 60s with exponential backoff on repeated failures rather than immediate permanent relaxation.
Per-tenant fairness cap set initially to 20% of region headroom during grace period; to be tuned from canary metrics.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Fail-open increases risk of quota over-consumption and potential cost exposure. Mitigation: bounded per-tenant caps + SLO-driven headroom calculation.

Tradeoff: Adding coordination between regions improves fairness but increases complexity and coupling; design favors eventual safety by keeping the coordinator lightweight and tolerant to partitioning.
Risk: Telemetry during outages may contain PII/tenant IDs; security review required before enabling high-cardinality metrics in prod.
Tradeoff: Using soft-credits avoids hard rejects but makes billing accuracy harder; finance must accept small reconciliation window.
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator and decay behavior
Integration tests simulating limiter process crash and RPC errors
Staging chaos: network partition between limiter and control-plane + limiter OOM kill
Canary in two regions for 48h with synthetic traffic and real customer shadowing
Post-canary load test at 2x typical regional burst to validate fairness caps
monitoring_and_alerting: SLO delta alerts: if availability drops >1.5% or p99 latency increases >25ms during canary, auto-roll back
Pager alert: grace_period_entered for >120s without health recovery
Audit log entry for every grace admission decision for post-mortem analysis
